RC6.gate1_irp_source: IrpTransmogrifier IrpProtocols.xml @c945e76 L2143-L2145 (verbatim), whose documentation calls it the first member of the RC6 family, technically RC6-0-16. DecodeIR's documentation (hifi-remote.com/johnsfine/DecodeIR.html, retrieved 2026-10-03) gives the same frame as '{36k,444,msb}<-1,1|1,-1>(6,-2,1:1,0:3,<-2,2|2,-2>(T:1),D:8,F:8,^107m)+', with '+' where IrpTransmogrifier has '*,T=1-T'. RC6.gate2a_structural_vector: bengtmartensson/IrpTransmogrifier @c945e76 src/test/java/org/harctoolbox/analyze/BiphaseWithDoubleToggleDecoderNGTest.java L27-L32 (D=255, F=0, both toggle states) and BiphaseDecoderNGTest.java L23-L26 (D=120, F=3): three published microsecond sequences, each asserted to decode to the stated fields. The encoder reproduces all three to the microsecond (tests/test_rc6.py): two end on a mark, one on a space, and both toggle states occur. Weaker than a published constant table: the sequences are exact multiples of the unit and appear to be this tool's own output, so they verify layout, the double-width trailer and the 107 ms extent, not that a receiver accepts them

RCA-38.gate2a_structural_vector: bengtmartensson/IrpTransmogrifier @c945e76 src/test/teaserfiles/RCA-38.ict and RCA-38.exp -- an irscope capture of an RCA remote, 31 keys, each asserted to decode to RCA-38 {D=15,F=...}. Cited, not vendored (GPL-3.0 test data of another project); tools/philips_capture_audit.py --irpt DIR reproduces the audit: every key's 24 bits decode to the .exp fields with the complement half intact, and this encoder's frame is within 12% or 150 us of every duration. A capture carries instrument bias and one remote's tolerances, so it verifies layout and ratios rather than absolute durations -- and its durations sit uniformly 1.085 times the IRP's (marks and spaces alike, so a 500 us unit against 460), a disagreement CITATIONS.md records
